newsitem.title: USA: Clinton tells Japan trade gap growing fast.
newsitem.headline: Clinton tells Japan trade gap growing fast.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton told Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Thursday that the trade gap between the two countries was seen growing rapidly, a Japanese spokesman said.
Clinton told Hashimoto he was concerned about that, the official said.

But the U.S. president, meeting the Japanese prime minister in Denver before a summit of the G7 group of industrialized countries and Russia, said he thought that expanding domestic demand and a program of deregulation, introduced by Hashimoto during the meeting, were important in addressing the problem of trade.
The Japanese official said Japan handed a note to the U.S. explaining that Japan's trade surplus was not likely to rise substantially in the medium term.

In the talks about the trade imbalance, Hashimoto was quoted by the official as saying that Japan's trade surplus in May rose more than 200 percent from a year earlier, but currency markets reacted to the figures prudently. The dollar edged down against the yen on Wednesday when the May trade data were announced.
